newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Major fraud trial begins in southern Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Major fraud trial begins in southern Vietnam.

text.p: Vietnam began what was billed as its biggest ever fraud trial on Wednesday as eight people appeared before a court in Ho Chi Minh City on charges related to deception and massive embezzlement of public funds.
State newspapers said some 18 people including 11 government officials had originally been implicated in the case, which involved at least $12 million and a large quantity of gold.
However, the lead defendant, Tran Xuan Hoa, was absent from the trial.
Court officials said she had fled across the border into Cambodia in 1994 as the police investigation into the case closed in on her.
Details of the allegations made against both Hoa and her fellow defendants were not available.

But Ho Chi Minh City's Thanh Nien newspaper said the charges included fraudulent appropriation of socialist and citizens' property, and violation of state regulations on economic management causing serious consequences.
The trial is the first major fraud case this year and comes at a time of increasing concern over corruption and other economic crimes in Vietnam.
According to a report issued by an independent consultancy last year the communist country is one of the most graft-ridden in Asia.
Government officials have responded by calling for tough measures to tackle the problem, raising concerns that the corruption issue may be acquiring political overtones.
Last year saw the first known instances in Vietnam's recent history in which the death penalty was carried out against people accused of economic crimes.
Court officials said the case was expected to last three days.
